title: Can Hardwood Floors Be Installed Over a Concrete Slab?
meta: Yes, hardwood can go over a concrete slab: engineered glued or floated, or solid over plywood, after a moisture test. Wills Flooring explains each method.
keywords: hardwood floors over concrete slab, can you install hardwood on concrete, engineered hardwood glue down concrete, solid hardwood over concrete plywood subfloor, concrete moisture test hardwood, Edmonds WA basement hardwood
offers: Hardwood floor installation, engineered or solid

blocks.lead: Yes. Hardwood can be installed over a concrete slab, but only as engineered hardwood glued or floated directly on the concrete, or as solid hardwood over a plywood subfloor built on top of the slab, and only after the slab passes a moisture test.
blocks.detail: Wills Flooring installs all three methods at $3.25 per sq ft for labor. The slab itself adds cost that a wood-subfloor house does not have: moisture testing, a vapor barrier or moisture-mitigation coating, sometimes leveling, and for solid wood a full plywood layer. Here is how to choose.

blocks.html: In Edmonds this question comes from two kinds of houses. Hillside homes in Seaview, Westgate and up toward Perrinville have daylight basements poured into the slope, and owners want the family room down there to match the oak upstairs. And a good number of 1950s to 70s ramblers in Esperance and near the Bowl were built slab-on-grade, so the whole main floor is concrete under the carpet. Both can have hardwood. Neither can have it the way you would install it over plywood.

blocks.text: Three ways to put hardwood on concrete

items.title: Glue-down engineered
items.text: Planks are set in a moisture-cure urethane adhesive troweled onto the slab. Many adhesives double as a vapor barrier. Solid feel, no hollow sound, works with radiant heat, and it is the standard for daylight basements. Slab must be flat and tested first.

items.title: Floating engineered
items.text: Click-lock or glued-edge planks float over a pad and a 6 mil poly vapor barrier. Quick, forgiving of minor slab imperfections, easy to repair. Can sound hollow, and wide planks may flex. Good for bedrooms and bonus rooms, less ideal for a large open basement.

items.title: Plywood subfloor, then nail-down
items.text: A vapor barrier goes down, then 3/4 in plywood is fastened to the slab or laid as a floating double layer, then solid hardwood is nailed to it. Adds about 1 1/2 in of height, real cost, and still leaves solid wood exposed to slab moisture. We recommend it only when matching existing solid floors is the goal.

Efflorescence (white mineral dust), dark patches, peeling paint on the slab or a musty smell are all signs of a slab that is passing water. In Edmonds basements dug into wet hillsides, we see it often.
An 18 in square of plastic taped to the slab for 24 to 72 hours. Condensation or a dark spot underneath means moisture is moving. A cheap, useful first screen, not a pass.

items.d: Step 3 · Calcium chloride or in-situ RH probes
items.text: The tests manufacturers actually require. Calcium chloride measures vapor emission in pounds per 1,000 sq ft per 24 hours; most floors allow 3 lb. RH probes drilled into the slab typically need to read 75 percent or lower.
items.note: Fail either, and the floor warranty is void without mitigation

items.text: Pass: proceed with the method you chose. Marginal: add a moisture-mitigation epoxy or a vapor-barrier adhesive. Fail badly: fix the drainage problem first, or choose a floor that does not care about water.

blocks.text: What the slab adds to the bill

items.html: Moisture testing. We do the plastic-sheet screen at the estimate. Calcium chloride or RH probe kits are a modest cost and take one to three days before install.
Adhesive or vapor barrier. Urethane adhesive with an integrated moisture barrier costs more per gallon than plain adhesive but replaces a separate mitigation step on most slabs.
Moisture-mitigation epoxy. For slabs that read high, a rolled epoxy coating brings them into spec. This is the biggest single extra on a wet Edmonds hillside basement.
Leveling. Glue-down floors need the slab flat to about 3/16 in over 10 ft. Self-leveling compound is priced by the bag and the area.
Plywood subfloor for solid wood. Material plus fastening labor plus the height adjustments at doors, stairs and toilets. This is why we steer most slab jobs to engineered.
The flooring itself. Quoted separately once you pick a sample. We are a Metropolitan Hardwood distributor and bring the boards to your house.

blocks.text: When to say no to hardwood on the slab

a.title: Hardwood on concrete makes sense when
items: The slab passes a real moisture test or can be mitigated
The space is finished living area, not a utility basement
You want the room to match hardwood elsewhere in the house
Drainage around the foundation is in good shape

b.title: Pick vinyl plank or tile when
items: The basement has ever had standing water or seeps in heavy rain
Efflorescence or peeling paint shows the slab is wet year-round
A sump pump, water heater or washer sits in the same open space
You would need to skip the moisture test to make the budget work

blocks.title: Edmonds basements deserve a warning:
blocks.text: Hillside lots between the Bowl and Perrinville sit on wet, clay-heavy ground, and a slab that is bone dry in August can read wet in February. We test in the season you are installing, we tell you the number, and if it fails we will say so rather than glue down a floor that will cup by spring. Read the crawlspace version of this question if your house has a wood subfloor instead.

faq.q: Can solid hardwood be installed directly on concrete?
faq.a: No. Solid hardwood must be nailed to a wood subfloor, and it cannot be glued or floated reliably because it moves too much with humidity. To use solid over a slab, a vapor barrier and a plywood subfloor are installed first, which adds height and cost. Engineered hardwood is the direct-to-concrete option.

faq.q: Do you need a vapor barrier under hardwood on concrete?
faq.a: Yes, always. Concrete constantly passes ground moisture as vapor, even when it feels dry. Floating floors use a 6 mil poly sheet under the pad. Glue-down floors use an adhesive with an integrated moisture barrier or a separate epoxy coating. Skipping it is the main cause of cupped floors over slabs.

faq.q: How do you test a concrete slab for moisture before hardwood?
faq.a: A plastic sheet taped to the slab for a day or two is the quick screen. The tests manufacturers require are calcium chloride, which measures vapor emission and usually must read 3 lb or less, or in-situ RH probes, which typically must read 75 percent or below. We do the screen at the estimate.

faq.q: Is glue-down or floating engineered hardwood better over concrete?
faq.a: Glue-down feels more solid, avoids hollow sounds and suits large open rooms and radiant heat. Floating is faster, more forgiving of slight unevenness and easier to repair. For an Edmonds daylight basement family room we usually recommend glue-down; for a bedroom or bonus room either works.

faq.q: Can hardwood go in a basement that has flooded before?
faq.a: We do not recommend it. A slab that has taken standing water will do so again, and no hardwood warranty covers flooding. Fix the drainage first, and even then consider vinyl plank for that space. If the water problem is truly solved and the slab tests dry for a full wet season, revisit hardwood.
